units.content: Experimental program tests whether invariant-preserving compression corresponds to measurable adaptive-intelligence differences.
Systems discovering reusable causal structures are predicted to achieve greater controllable future reach than memorization, brute-force search or fixed-policy systems.
Proposes representation-compression, causal-generalization, counterfactual-steering, adaptation/self-modification and viability-kernel benchmark categories.
Source gives expected structural ordering/profiles for Random, Shortest Path and CGET agents; expectations are not observations.
Proposed collected metrics include success, future complexity, steering, causal fidelity, operator closure, identity preservation, transition stability, Psi_stable and Theta*.
Lists no-compression-advantage, no-agency-distinction, no-value-stability-benefit and metric-redundancy falsifiers.
Phase 1 formalization marked completed; Phase 2 toy validation explicitly in progress; MazeWorld/baselines/metric implementation are not reported as completed measured experiments.
Defines baseline comparisons intended to test whether CGET explains differences beyond prediction, reward, search or fixed control.
Defines Random, Fixed Policy, Search, RL, World Model and CGET agent comparison classes with source-described purposes.
Tables of expected compression/causal/control/adaptation/identity profiles are predictions, not measured agent properties.
Predicts CGET advantages under distribution shift, compositional generalization and constrained self-modification.
Primary falsification asks whether compression, steering, identity constraints and combined metrics add predictive value over baselines.
Experimental comparison framework with expected behavior; no baseline benchmark execution is reported in this file.
Defines tests under which CGET components would be unnecessary, non-predictive or structurally wrong.
Test hypotheses cover causal compression, closure, value closure, identity preservation, transition stability, agency, representation vs scaling and alignment without internal models.
Each hypothesis is paired with comparison/falsification conditions; strongest falsifier is robust superhuman recursive intelligence without the proposed structural components.
Future experiments should measure compression, intervention accuracy, composition, core drift, steering, transition divergence and controlled future expansion.
Falsification design; no falsification test execution or result is reported.
Document explicitly demonstrates the expected reporting format of a toy benchmark run.
Source explicitly states all displayed values are synthetic examples and are not experimental results.
Synthetic configuration displays MazeWorld v0.1, 100 episodes, max 100 steps and seeds 1-5 as example report fields, not a provenance-backed run record.
Displayed success, steps, future complexity, steering, representation, causal fidelity, closure, identity, Theta* and Psi_stable values are synthetic output examples.
Narrative interprets the synthetic ordering Random < Shortest Path < CGET; it carries no empirical-support effect.
Lists conditions an actual benchmark could use to challenge CGET and planned benchmark extensions.
Current state: toy benchmark specification; required next step: run actual experiments and replace synthetic values with measured results.
Frozen .py blob is literally wrapped in Markdown triple-backtick fences; as stored it is not directly executable Python despite the .py extension.
Embedded code describes an intended toy benchmark runner over identical environments and explicitly says it is not a claim of measuring general intelligence.
Intended configuration uses GRID_SIZE=10, MAX_STEPS=100 and seeds 1-5.
Defines evaluation helpers, reachable/steerable estimators, CGET metric aggregation, agent averaging and report printing.

Intended runner calls APIs absent/incompatible with frozen MazeWorld/agents: MazeWorld(size,seed), env.step(action) tuple return, enumerate_future_states(), agent.act(), and agent.enumerate_controlled_states(). Integrated benchmark executability is therefore not established even after hypothetical fence removal.
Identity/transition and several composite inputs are fixed or derived from coarse success/bandwidth substitutions rather than measured CGET constructs.
Intended code prints final CGET comparison if runnable; no frozen execution log/output establishes that this behavior occurred.
Defines seven toy-agent experiment designs to isolate representation, causality, closure, value stability, agency and self-modification mechanisms.
Specifies Maze Compression, Physics Discovery, Operator Composition, Value Closure, Identity Preservation, Agency-vs-Complexity and Self-Improving CGET agent designs.
Each toy design includes expected CGET behavior such as representation transfer, causal intervention robustness, closure and identity-preserving agency expansion.
Comparison table assigns expected qualitative properties to hypothetical toy agents; not a measured benchmark table.
Toy-agent specification/progression, not an execution record.
Frozen .py blob is wrapped in Markdown code fences and is not directly executable Python as stored.
Embedded code self-describes as minimum viable toy implementation of CGET structural differences, not a full intelligence model.
Implements intended transition-model learning, danger-state memory, action operators, causal prediction and BFS planning over learned transitions.
World-learning exploration repeatedly takes the first available action for up to 20 episodes/100 steps; this is a toy implementation choice, not validated discovery procedure.
Evaluation counts episode success/failure/steps after a representation-learning phase.
Returned agency_bandwidth=.75, representation_compression=.80, causal_fidelity=.85, operator_closure=.70 and identity_preservation=1.0 are programmed constants, not measurements derived by the code.
Intended direct run prints benchmark fields; no frozen run output is present.
Frozen .py blob is wrapped in Markdown code fences and is not directly executable Python as stored.
Embedded code specifies a fixed toy MazeWorld for reachability, agency, viability and self-modification concepts.
Defines fixed grid, State, no-argument MazeWorld constructor, reset, valid_position, step(state,action), available_actions and rendering.
reachable_space(depth=10) is bounded graph exploration and viability_kernel excludes the single danger state; source calls viability approximation simplified.
Frozen API has no size/seed constructor arguments and no enumerate_future_states method, which conflicts with run_all_agents.py intended interface.
Intended direct run prints initial world, reachable count, viability-kernel count and available actions; no stored execution output.
Frozen .py blob is wrapped in Markdown code fences and is not directly executable Python as stored.
Embedded code maps CGET concepts to toy operational measurements and explicitly calls them experimental proxies, not final definitions.
Implements ratios for representation compression, causal fidelity and operator closure.
Implements reachable/steerable counts and steering-bandwidth ratio.
Identity/core-loss and transition-stability functions use scalar absolute differences as toy approximations to richer divergence-based constructs.
Implements agency_ratio and multiplicative cget_score plus intended report printer; implementation does not validate the proxies.
Frozen .py blob is wrapped in Markdown code fences and is not directly executable Python as stored.
Embedded code specifies RandomAgent as lower baseline with no model/abstraction/planning/viability preservation.
Implements random choice among available actions and episode success/failure/step counting on MazeWorld.
Evaluation returns agency_bandwidth=0, representation_compression=0 and causal_fidelity=0 by programmed interpretation, not measured estimators.
Intended direct run prints evaluation values; no execution record is stored.
Toy baseline implementation text; execution and empirical baseline performance are not established.

Embedded code specifies a breadth-first shortest-path baseline for optimization without learned representation/causal abstraction/self-modification.
Implements BFS path search and episode success/failure/step counting against MazeWorld.
Evaluation hard-codes agency=.25, representation compression=.10, causal fidelity=.50 and operator closure=.10 rather than measuring them.
Intended direct run prints benchmark fields; no execution record is stored.
Toy baseline implementation text; benchmark performance and CGET metric values are not empirically established.
